articles.title: Nonoperative treatment of Achilles tendon rupture with 6- versus 8-week protocol: a single-center cohort study from Finland.
articles.authors: Happonen V, Koivisto A, Harkonen A, Kroger H
articles.study_type: Single-centre cohort study comparing two treatment protocols
articles.population: Patients with Achilles tendon rupture treated at a university hospital in Finland
articles.sample_size: 479 Achilles tendon ruptures, 429 treated nonoperatively (251 with 8-week protocol, 228 with 6-week protocol)
articles.outcomes: Re-rupture rates, need for surgery, treatment failure, postoperative complications
articles.take_home: A shorter 6-week nonoperative treatment protocol for Achilles tendon rupture had similar re-rupture rates and treatment failure compared to the traditional 8-week protocol. The authors suggest the shorter protocol may be effective, though larger studies in different populations are needed to confirm this finding.

articles.title: Plate-Based Operative Management of Medial Malleolar Stress Fractures in High-Level Basketball Players: A Short Report.
articles.authors: O'Malley E, Kim J, O'Malley M
articles.population: High-level basketball players with medial malleolar stress fractures
articles.outcomes: Radiographic union, return to play, need for additional surgery
articles.take_home: All 10 basketball players achieved bone healing with plate-based surgery. Nine returned to competitive play within 4 months, though one player needed revision surgery after a re-injury.

articles.title: Tibiotalocalcaneal Arthrodesis: Deformity Correction in Medically Comorbid Patients.
articles.authors: Alecxih AG, Klouda CB, Duff JR, Parker RP, Wilson AW, Doty JF
articles.population: High-risk patients with end-stage ankle and hindfoot pathologies undergoing tibiotalocalcaneal arthrodesis, including those with diabetes and severe deformities
articles.outcomes: Postoperative complications, revision surgery rates, amputation rates, union rates, and hardware removal requirements
articles.take_home: Intramedullary nail surgery had a lower revision rate (4%) compared with open plating (28%), suggesting it may be more reliable in high-risk patients with diabetes and severe deformities. Both techniques had similar overall complication rates (29% versus 39%), though open plating required more revision procedures.

articles.title: The effect of restoring the native ankle on clinical outcome and range of motion in total ankle arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Hintermann B, Susdorf R, Chelli S, Peterhans US, Ruiz R
articles.study_type: Retrospective review of prospectively collected data
articles.population: Patients who had primary total ankle replacement surgery
articles.sample_size: 178 patients selected from 471 (89 best outcomes, 89 worst outcomes)
articles.outcomes: Range of motion, clinical outcomes, implant positioning measurements (talar height, talar radius, tibiotalar joint line level, anteroposterior talus position, lateral tibial surface angle)
articles.take_home: Patients with better outcomes after ankle replacement had greater increase in talar height and better range of motion, but implant positioning alone did not explain the differences between good and poor outcomes, suggesting other factors like soft tissue condition also matter.
